Ms Advanced Excel Syllabus.docx:
ADVANCED EXCEL COURSE (DURATION -45 DAYS ) / 40 HOURS
TOPICS COVERED (ADVANCED FEATURES OF MS EXCEL)This advanced Excel course prepares students with the skills to utilize powerful Excel features. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply these advanced techniques in an office environment, maximizing productivity and efficiency.
Basic Microsoft Excel
Spreadsheet Basics
Understand the fundamental components of an Excel spreadsheet, including cells, rows, and columns.
Creating, Editing, Saving, and Printing Spreadsheets
Learn how to create, modify, save, and print spreadsheets for effective data management.
Working with Functions & Formulas
Use Excel’s built-in functions and formulas to perform calculations and analyze data efficiently.
Graphically Representing Data: Charts & Graphs
Create various charts and graphs to visually represent and interpret data trends and patterns.
Analyzing Data: Data Menu, Subtotal, Filtering Data
Utilize the Data menu options, apply subtotals, and filter data to enhance analysis and make informed decisions.
Formatting Worksheets
Apply different formatting techniques to improve the presentation and readability of your spreadsheets.
Securing & Protecting Spreadsheets
Use password protection and other security features to safeguard your data and prevent unauthorized access.
TYPE OF FORMULAS & FUNCTIONS 
Using the Function Wizard
Explore Excel's Function Wizard to easily insert and apply functions in your worksheets.
Common Functions
Learn to use basic functions like AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA, ROUND, and INT for data analysis.
Nested Functions
Combine multiple functions within one formula to perform more complex calculations.
Naming Cells/Ranges/Constants
Assign names to specific cells, ranges, or constants for easier reference in formulas.
Relative, Absolute, and Mixed Cell References
Understand the differences between relative, absolute, and mixed references, and when to use them in formulas (e.g., >, <, = operators).
Logical Functions Using IF, AND, OR, NOT
Apply logical functions to evaluate conditions and return results based on specified criteria.
The LOOKUP Function
Use the LOOKUP function to search for specific values in a data range and retrieve corresponding information.
Date and Time Functions
Work with date and time-related functions to manipulate and analyze time-based data.
DATA ANALYSIS IN EXCEL
Sub Total Reports, Auto Filter
Use Subtotal reports and Auto Filter to organize and analyze data by grouping and filtering.
Password Protecting Worksheets
Secure your worksheets by applying password protection to prevent unauthorized access and modifications.
Linking Multiple Sheets
Create links between different sheets within the same workbook to efficiently share and analyze data.
Sheet Referencing
Use referencing techniques to pull data from different sheets within a workbook or across multiple workbooks.
Linking Between Word/Excel/PowerPoint
Link data between Excel, Word, and PowerPoint to maintain consistency and ensure smooth integration across Microsoft Office applications.
Functions
LOOKUP: Retrieve data from a specified range.
VLOOKUP & HLOOKUP: Perform vertical and horizontal lookups to find data in tables.
COUNTIF & SUMIF: Count or sum values based on specific criteria.
What-If Analysis & Goal Seek
Use What-If analysis to explore different scenarios and use Goal Seek to find the right input to achieve a desired result.
Pivot Tables
Create Pivot Tables to summarize, analyze, explore, and present large data sets effectively.
Nested IF Functions
Apply nested IF statements to evaluate multiple conditions and return results accordingly.
Reporting
Generate customized reports from your data to share insights and support decision-making.
Character Functions
Use text functions (e.g., LEFT, RIGHT, MID) to manipulate and extract information from text data.
Date Functions
Work with date-related functions to calculate durations, differences, and other time-based calculations.
Age Calculations
Calculate age based on date of birth using date functions.
Consolidation of Data
Combine data from multiple ranges or sheets into a single summary to simplify reporting and analysis.
Data Validation
Set up data validation rules to ensure that only valid data is entered into your worksheet.
Macros
Automate repetitive tasks by recording and running Macros to increase efficiency.
MACROS IN EXCEL
Definition and Use
A macro is a sequence of recorded actions or commands that automate repetitive tasks in Excel. Macros help save time and ensure consistency by performing tasks with a single click.
Recording a Macro
Learn how to record a macro by capturing a series of actions in Excel, which can then be replayed to repeat the tasks automatically.
Assigning a Macro
Assign a macro to a button, keyboard shortcut, or other triggers to make it easily accessible for running at any time.
Running a Macro
Execute the recorded macro to perform the saved actions instantly, streamlining your workflow and improving efficiency.
ADVANCED EXCEL FUNCTIONS AND CALCULATIONS
PPMT (Principal Payment)
Calculate the principal portion of a loan payment based on a specific period using the PPMT function.
IPMT (Interest Payment)
Use the IPMT function to calculate the interest portion of a loan payment for a given period.
DB (Declining Balance)
The DB function is used to calculate depreciation using the declining balance method.
SLN (Straight Line Depreciation)
Calculate the depreciation of an asset evenly over its useful life using the SLN function.
FV (Future Value)
The FV function helps calculate the future value of an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.
PV (Present Value)
Calculate the present value of an investment or loan with fixed payments and a constant interest rate using the PV function.
Simple Interest
Use the formula to calculate simple interest based on principal, rate, and time:Simple Interest=P×R×TSimple Interest=P×R×T
Compound Interest
Use the formula to calculate compound interest based on principal, rate, number of times interest is compounded, and time:Compound Interest=P(1+rn)nt−PCompound Interest=P(1+nr​)nt−P
Attendance Cum Salary Calculation
Track employee attendance and calculate salaries based on worked hours, attendance records, and pay rates.
Stock Calculation
Use Excel to track stock prices, calculate average costs, and analyze investment returns using functions like AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, and custom formulas.
DIFFERENT TYPES OF CHARTS IN EXCEL
1. Column Chart (2D & 3D)
Feature: Displays data as vertical bars, useful for comparing values across categories.
2D: Simple column chart with a straightforward vertical bar representation.
3D: Adds depth and perspective to columns for a more visually appealing design.
2. Bar Chart (2D & 3D)
Feature: Displays data as horizontal bars, ideal for comparing categories when the category labels are long.
2D: Basic horizontal bars for easy comparison across categories.
3D: Adds depth to the bars for a more dynamic look.
3. Line Chart (2D & 3D)
Feature: Shows trends over time (continuous data) with a connected series of data points.
2D: A simple line chart for displaying trends and changes in data.
3D: Adds a three-dimensional view to the line, providing a more visually engaging representation.
4. Pie Chart (2D & 3D)
Feature: Displays parts of a whole as slices, useful for showing percentages or proportions of categories.
2D: Simple, flat pie chart that visually represents the proportion of each segment.
3D: Adds depth and visual effect to the pie chart, making it more eye-catching.
5. Area Chart (2D & 3D)
Feature: Similar to line charts but with the area below the line filled, showing cumulative totals over time.
2D: A filled area chart, used to emphasize the magnitude of values over time.
3D: Adds a three-dimensional effect to the filled areas, making the data stand out more dramatically.
6. Combo Chart (2D & 3D)
Feature: Combines two chart types (e.g., column and line) to show different types of data together in one chart.
2D: Combines two different chart types in 2D for effective data comparison.
3D: Adds depth to the combined chart for better visualization.
